c.tagline: Cafe culture and Austro-Hungarian charm beneath a medieval Upper Town.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; Uber and Bolt are widely used and often cheaper than street taxis (Radio Taxi Zagreb, Eko Taxi, Cammeo).

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the trams and the areas around the main train station and Ban Jelačić Square, especially in tourist season.

hood_desc: Zagreb's cobblestoned medieval hilltop — St. Mark's Church with its tiled roof, the Stone Gate, Lotrscak Tower and the Museum of Broken Relationships, lit by gas lamps at night. Romantic and historic, though steep and hilly; best for sightseeing and old-world atmosphere.

The flat 19th-century centre and its 'Green Horseshoe' of parks and museums, running from Ban Jelacic Square down past the main train station. Elegant Austro-Hungarian streets full of cafes, shops, theatres and nightlife — the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers.

The ecclesiastical old core around the twin-spired Zagreb Cathedral and the bustling Dolac farmers' market with its red umbrellas. Historic and central, threaded by the Tkalciceva cafe-and-bar street and traditional restaurants — great for sights and food.

A leafy, residential district just west of the centre off the Ilica shopping street, known for its Sunday antiques market and neighbourhood cafes. Quieter and more local, yet an easy walk or tram ride from the main sights.

A recreational lake district southwest of the centre — 'Zagreb's sea' — with beaches, cycling and rowing by day and a strip of lakeside clubs by night. Green and relaxed, well away from the tourist core; suited to longer or active stays.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Daytime trams and buses run about 4am-midnight, after which an extensive night-tram and night-bus network runs all night.
transit.note: The funicular linking the Lower and Upper Towns is one of the world's shortest, at just 66 metres.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from the ZET app, Tisak/iNovine kiosks or ticket machines, or tap a contactless bank card on trams and buses; a 30-minute ticket is about EUR 0.53, a 60-minute ticket EUR 0.93 (EUR 1.33 from the driver) and a 24-hour day pass about EUR 2.65. Validate paper tickets on board.

bus: Zagreb Bus Station (Autobusni kolodvor; FlixBus & Croatian intercity coaches)
train: Zagreb Glavni kolodvor (main station; EC/IC trains to Vienna, Ljubljana, Budapest and the Croatian coast)

transit.m: Croatia Airlines shuttle bus to Zagreb Bus Station (~35 min)
ZET city bus 290 to Kvaternik Square (~45 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants for good service; round up taxi fares and small bills.
